arguments.content:
The Maltese is renowned for its luxurious, silky white coat, but that beauty requires dedicated, regular grooming to prevent mats, tangles, and staining. With the right products, tools, and technique, you can keep your Maltese looking showroom-ready at home. The entire bath-to-finish process typically takes between 1.5 and 2.5 hours, depending on coat length and condition.

1. **Gather the correct products and tools.** Before you begin, assemble everything you will need so you are not scrambling mid-bath. You will want a tearless whitening shampoo (such as TropiClean Bright White or Burt's Bees Tearless Puppy Shampoo), a high-quality detangling or moisturizing conditioner (such as The Stuff Conditioner or Chris Christensen Ice on Ice), a high-velocity blow dryer (also called a forced-air dryer), a pin brush with rounded tips, a steel "greyhound-style" comb with both fine and coarse teeth, a slicker brush, grooming scissors or thinning shears, a cotton ball or ear-cleaning solution, a non-slip bath mat, and several absorbent towels. Having a detangling spray or leave-in conditioner on hand is also highly recommended.

2. **Brush out the entire coat thoroughly.** Never bathe a Maltese without brushing first — water tightens existing mats and makes them nearly impossible to remove. Use the slicker brush first to work through the outer coat, then follow with the steel comb to find and gently work out any hidden tangles, paying close attention to the armpits, behind the ears, under the collar area, and around the tail. This step alone can take 20–30 minutes on a longer coat.

3. **Trim excess hair if needed.** Before the bath is an ideal time to trim the hair around the paw pads, the sanitary area, and any severely matted sections that brushing could not resolve. Keeping paw-pad hair short also helps prevent slipping in the tub.

4. **Prepare the bath area.** Place a non-slip mat in the tub or sink. Fill it with lukewarm water (about 37 °C / 98 °F). Maltese are small and can chill easily, so make sure the room is warm and draft-free. Have your shampoo diluted in a squeeze bottle (a ratio of roughly 1 part shampoo to 3–5 parts water works well for even distribution).

5. **Wet the coat completely.** Using a handheld sprayer or a gentle stream of water, thoroughly saturate the coat from the neck down. Avoid directing water into the ears and eyes. The Maltese coat is dense enough that it can repel water at first, so be patient and make sure the water reaches the skin.

6. **Apply and work in the shampoo.** Apply the diluted whitening shampoo and massage it deep into the coat in long, downward strokes. Work from the neck to the tail and down the legs. Use the tearless formula on the face, gently lathering with your fingers or a soft face cloth. Allow the shampoo to sit for 3–5 minutes if the label permits, which gives the brightening agents time to work. Rinse thoroughly — residual shampoo is one of the leading causes of dry, itchy skin and dull coat.

7. **Apply conditioner.** Work a generous amount of moisturizing conditioner or detangling conditioner through the coat, focusing on the areas most prone to matting (ears, armpits, belly, and behind the legs). Leave it on for 3–5 minutes to allow it to soften and penetrate the hair shafts, then rinse completely. A leave-in conditioner or detangling spray can be lightly misted on after the final rinse for extra protection.

8. **Towel-dry gently.** Remove excess water by blotting and squeezing the coat with an absorbent towel — do not rub vigorously, as this causes tangles. A microfiber towel or chamois works particularly well. Gently squeeze the ears and tail. You should remove as much moisture as possible before moving to the dryer, as this cuts down drying time significantly. Expect this step to take about 5–10 minutes.

9. **Blow-dry with a high-velocity dryer.** This is the most critical step for a smooth, mat-free finish. Set the dryer on a warm (not hot) setting. Hold the nozzle close to the coat and work in small sections, brushing or combing each section taut as you dry it. Always dry in the direction of hair growth. Start at the back legs and work forward, saving the head for last. A high-velocity dryer is strongly preferred over a human hair dryer because it forces water out of the coat quickly without relying on extreme heat that can damage fine Maltese hair. This drying phase typically takes 30–45 minutes.

10. **Final brush-out and comb-through.** Once the coat is completely dry, brush through with the pin brush and then run the steel comb through every section to confirm there are no remaining tangles or mats. The coat should feel silky and fall smoothly. Finish with a light mist of leave-in conditioner or a coat-shine spray for added softness and protection. Trim any stray hairs around the eyes or feet for a polished look. This final detail work usually takes 10–15 minutes.

In total, expect to spend roughly 1.5 to 2.5 hours from start to finish, with much of that time devoted to brushing and blow drying. Regular baths every 2–3 weeks, combined with daily brushing sessions of 10–15 minutes between baths, will keep the Maltese coat healthy, tangle-free, and beautifully white.
